A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LoRM research. Their main text, equations, algorithms, figures, tables, and appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial experimental revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original FCIL experiments on CIFAR-100, ImageNet-R, and EuroSAT, including accuracy comparisons, convergence and component analyses, and standard deviations.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments on six vision datasets and the Out-of-Scope language dataset, alongside retained ablations and uncertainty tables.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain alternating A/B optimization, closed-form client aggregation, diagonal Gram communication, and task-residual merging. The new backbones and revised hyperparameters do not introduce a documented change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: v2 retains all three original datasets and adds ImageNet-A, Cars-196, CUB-200, and Out-of-Scope. Coverage expands to natural adversarial images, fine-grained specialization, and 150-class textual intent classification.

E2.justification: FedProto replaces DER++ in the retained vision comparisons, and TIES-Merging is newly evaluated against LoRM on Out-of-Scope. The other vision comparators remain, including methods previously reported in v1 appendix Table C.

E3.justification: Appendix D revises numerous settings: for example, CIFAR-100 at beta=0.5 changes LoRM's rank from 16 to 1 and learning rate from 1e-3 to 3e-4. EuroSAT preprocessing changes from explicit bicubic resizing to no additional preprocessing. Added experiments introduce ten communication rounds for ImageNet-A/Cars-196 and T5-small for Out-of-Scope. These are reported setting changes, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The component ablation is retained as Table 4, but its RegMean reference scores change from 61.05/44.84 to 61.18/48.74 for ImageNet-R/EuroSAT. Figures 2–3 retain the convergence and alternating-versus-only-B analyses; moving the convergence discussion into Section 4.3 adds no new analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-run averages and standard deviations; v2 newly specifies different seeds without increasing the stated run count. Joint standard-deviation entries disappear from vision Tables A–B. The new Out-of-Scope Table C repeats LoRM's mean accuracies, leaving its intended uncertainty values unclear.

E6.justification: Most original benchmark means and standard deviations are replaced, and four datasets gain results. At ImageNet-R beta=0.05, LoRM/CCVR change from 70.18/71.83 to 66.45/60.38, reversing their reported ranking. Because settings also change, this is revised evidence rather than a controlled performance improvement. New Out-of-Scope results report LoRM accuracies of 84.78, 82.58, and 77.67.

T1.justification: The LoRA, VeRA, (IA)3, and classifier-merging derivations remain substantively unchanged. Appendix A clarifies N and repairs notation, including the stray theta in the W0 expansion and the ones-vector subscript, without changing assumptions, solutions, or proof logic.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the claims of closed-form LoRA merging, alternating optimization, and state-of-the-art FCIL performance. Expanded experiments support these existing contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 substantially revises the scientific interpretation. v1 emphasizes replay-memory benefits and L2P's prompt pool on EuroSAT; v2 instead emphasizes CODA-Prompt's generalization and suggests distillation is less effective than EWC there. New discussions explain specialization performance and attribute CCVR's poor language-task results to catastrophic forgetting.

D1.justification: v2 adds a reproduction-code link, preprocessing instructions for the added vision datasets, and hyperparameter specifications covering seven datasets. It newly distinguishes backbone and classifier Gram-decay settings. Conversely, explicit Joint learning rates and CODA-Prompt prompt-count entries from v1 are omitted.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds Context Optimization, CGIL, and HGP, alongside references supporting the new datasets, FedProto, and T5. The DER++ reference is removed. Positioning around RegMean-based closed-form LoRA merging remains intact; publication updates to existing references do not constitute new cited works.

P1.justification: Rewriting concentrates on experimental settings/results and selected related-work paragraphs. The convergence discussion moves into ablations, appendices C–D are reorganized, and acknowledgments and publication-status edits appear. The introduction, methodology, conclusion, and mathematical exposition remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Benchmark and uncertainty tables are substantially restructured into multi-dataset displays. EuroSAT comparisons formerly split between main text and appendix are consolidated, Out-of-Scope tables appear, and Appendix D replaces separate distribution-specific lists with tables containing parallel beta columns. Figures 1–3 retain their graphics, with caption edits.

improvement.justification: The added evaluations probe adversarial images, fine-grained recognition, and text, revealing applicability and competitive limits beyond v1's three vision datasets. Code-access information and richer implementation settings also help reproducibility. These gains are tempered by DER++'s removal, unreconciled main-result/ablation discrepancies, and Table C repeating LoRM means as standard deviations, limiting the overall quality improvement.
